contract_assessment.portable_typed_storage: SYCL 2020 revision 12 local_accessor creates DataT objects with indeterminate values when DataT is implicit-lifetime and device-supported. MatrixTile is an aggregate; its actual BFloat member array is written before use. The report correctly limits this to the portable typed-object contract and treats address_space_cast as an address-space conversion, not an alignment or lifetime repair.
contract_assessment.member_alignment: alignas(4) gives each MatrixTile complete object the type alignment. Passing that guarantee to values also requires the member offset to preserve 4-byte alignment. Current source asserts Q specialization alignment and size; it does not explicitly assert standard-layout/member offset and exact size for KV and probability specializations. R950 correctly leaves this as an explicit source-proof gap and recommends assertions for every specialization.
contract_assessment.offset_stride_arithmetic: Source calls use pointer-plus-stride overloads. Q offsets head*256+d, K offsets d*32+cell, P offsets head*32+c, and V offsets c*256+dim_base+j*16 are each multiples of 16 BF16 elements. Assuming sizeof(BFloat)==2 and aligned member bases, each offset is 32-byte aligned. Strides are 32 or 256 elements (64 or 512 bytes), both multiples of 8 and below 2^24 bytes. The 16-bit row_index rule is not invoked by these overloads.
contract_assessment.matrix_extension: The pinned Intel specification lists BMG G21/G31 BF16 A/B to FP32 accumulator combinations including 8x16x16 and states the base-pointer and stride restrictions. This is Intel experimental-extension behavior, not a core-SYCL guarantee; runtime query support does not establish the actual generated path.
contract_assessment.initialization_and_barriers: Static source review confirms every Q element, each full K/V tile, and each probability row is written before its first matrix load; barriers separate writers/readers and K/V tile reuse. Runtime cases exercise the produced path but do not replace that source ordering proof.
contract_assessment.alternatives: Separate MatrixTile accessors and one aggregate accessor with distinct real arrays are portable typed designs if member offsets and extents are asserted. group_local_memory_for_overwrite is accurately described as an Intel extension option requiring sycl::group and trivially destructible T. No alternative has a demonstrated B570 resource or speed advantage.
contract_assessment.resource_cost: The 28,160-byte local payload and 4,096-byte admission margin are source estimates. Accessor count, bundle layout, implementation rounding, occupancy, and performance remain compiler/runtime/device questions.

corrections.detail: LocalPayload hardcodes BF16 bytes as *2, while its arithmetic is independent of sizeof(BFloat). Add static_assert(sizeof(BFloat)==2), or derive the payload from sizeof(BFloat), so the admission calculation cannot silently diverge from the operand type. Current Intel BF16 path and passing build show no present failure.

Only the Q MatrixTile specialization currently has explicit size/alignment assertions. Keep 4-byte base alignment conditional on values member offset for Q/KV/P; add standard-layout, offsetof modulo 4, alignof, and exact-size assertions to all three before treating alignment as source-proven.

The updated caller in src/prefill/prefill.cpp:2601 selects qsa_bf16_prefix_optimized_batch for bf16_prefix_optimized. R950 is about that typed operand source; it does not infer general/default adoption.
